slides.title: Welcome to Safety and Hygiene
slides.content:
# Safety and Hygiene - Staying Safe and Healthy!

Your safety is the most important thing in the world. Learning safety rules can **save your life**!

## What You Will Learn:
- **Personal safety rules** to protect yourself
- **Hygiene practices** to stay clean and healthy
- **Emergency contacts** and what to do in emergencies
- **Safe behavior** at home and school

## Why Safety Matters:
- Accidents can happen **anywhere** and **anytime**
- Knowing safety rules helps you **avoid danger**
- Quick thinking in emergencies can **save lives**
- Being safe means you can continue to **play and learn happily**

## Why Hygiene Matters:
- Good hygiene keeps **diseases away**
- Clean habits make you feel **confident and fresh**
- Hygiene protects **you AND the people around you**

> **Golden Rule of Safety:** Always be **aware** of your surroundings and think **before** you act. Most accidents can be prevented!

slides.title: Safety at Home
slides.content:
# Safety at Home

Home is the safest place, but accidents can still happen if we are not careful.

## Kitchen Safety:
- **Never touch** hot pots, pans, or the stove
- Stay away from **sharp knives** and scissors
- Do not play near the **cooking area**
- Tell an adult if you see water **spilled** on the floor
- Never put your hand in a **running mixer or blender**

## Electrical Safety:
- **Never** touch electrical switches with wet hands
- Do not put **fingers or objects** into electrical sockets
- Stay away from **broken wires** or damaged plugs
- **Turn off** appliances when not in use
- Do not play with **electrical cords**

## Bathroom Safety:
- Use a **non-slip mat** in the bathroom
- Do not run on **wet floors**
- Keep **medicines** and cleaning products out of reach
- Always use **warm** water, not very hot water
- Lock the bathroom door when using it

## General Home Safety:
- Do not **climb** on furniture or counters
- Keep **toys** off the stairs
- Do not open the door to **strangers**
- Know where the **first aid kit** is
- Do not play with **matches or lighters**

> **Important Rule:** If you are unsure about something, ALWAYS ask an adult first!

slides.title: Safety at School
slides.content:
# Safety at School

School should be a safe and fun place for everyone!

## Classroom Safety:
- **Walk**, do not run, inside the classroom
- Sit **properly** on your chair (no leaning back)
- Handle **scissors** carefully (point them down when walking)
- Do not throw **objects** at others
- Keep your **bag** under the desk, not in the aisle

## Playground Safety:
- Always play in **designated areas**
- Follow the **rules** of each game
- Wait your **turn** on swings and slides
- Do not push or shove others
- Tell a teacher if **equipment** is broken
- Play on **soft ground**, not concrete when possible

## Science Lab Safety:
- Only touch things when the **teacher says so**
- Wear **safety goggles** when needed
- Never **taste or smell** chemicals directly
- Report **spills** or breakage immediately
- Wash your hands **after** experiments

## School Bus Safety:
- Stand in a **line** while waiting for the bus
- Do not put hands or head **out of the window**
- Stay **seated** while the bus is moving
- Wait for the bus to **stop completely** before getting off
- Cross the road in front of the bus, not behind

## Fire Drill Rules:
1. Stay **calm** and do not panic
2. Follow your teacher's **instructions**
3. Walk in a **line** to the assembly point
4. Do NOT go back for your **belongings**
5. Stay together and wait for the **all-clear**

> **Be a Safety Monitor:** If you see something unsafe at school, tell your teacher right away!

slides.title: Road Safety
slides.content:
# Road Safety - Stay Safe on the Roads!

Roads can be **dangerous** if you do not follow safety rules. Thousands of accidents happen every day.

## Rules for Pedestrians (Walking):

### Crossing the Road:
1. Always cross at a **zebra crossing** or traffic signal
2. **Look left, look right, look left again** before crossing
3. Wait for vehicles to **stop completely**
4. **Walk**, do not run, across the road
5. Make **eye contact** with drivers to make sure they see you

### Walking on the Road:
- Always walk on the **footpath (sidewalk)**
- If there is no footpath, walk on the **left side** facing traffic
- Wear **bright or reflective clothes** at night
- Do not use your **phone** while walking near roads
- Hold an adult's **hand** when crossing busy roads

## Traffic Signals:

| Light | Meaning |
|-------|--------|
| **Red** | STOP - Do not cross |
| **Yellow** | GET READY - Wait |
| **Green** | GO - Safe to cross (but still look!) |

## Bicycle Safety:
- Always wear a **helmet**
- Ride on the **correct side** of the road
- Use **hand signals** when turning
- Do not ride in the **dark** without lights
- Never ride **double** on a single bicycle

## Car Safety:
- Always wear your **seatbelt**
- Children should sit in the **back seat**
- Use a **car seat or booster** if you are small
- Do not distract the **driver**
- Never put body parts **outside** the window

> **Remember:** The road is NOT a playground. Always be alert and follow traffic rules!

slides.title: Water Safety
slides.content:
# Water Safety

Water is fun, but it can also be **dangerous**. Always follow water safety rules!

## Swimming Safety:
- **Never swim alone** - always have an adult watching
- Learn to **swim** - it is an important life skill
- Swim only in **designated, safe areas**
- Do not swim in **rivers or ponds** with strong currents
- Do not dive into **shallow water**
- Get out of the water if you feel **tired**

## At the Beach:
- Swim only where **lifeguards** are present
- Obey **warning flags** on the beach
- Be aware of **waves and currents**
- Never turn your **back** to the ocean
- Apply **sunscreen** to protect from sunburn

## At Home:
- Do not leave **buckets of water** uncovered (danger for small children)
- Do not run near a **swimming pool**
- Be careful in the **bathroom** (wet and slippery)
- Never leave young children **alone** near water

## What to Do If Someone Is Drowning:
1. **Shout for help** immediately
2. Call **emergency services**
3. Throw a **rope, float, or ring** if available
4. Do NOT jump in unless you are a **trained swimmer**
5. Stay calm and keep calling for **help**

## Flood Safety:
- **Stay away** from flooded areas
- Do not walk or play in **flood water**
- Flood water can carry **diseases** and hidden dangers
- Follow **official instructions** during floods

> **Safety First:** Even a few inches of water can be dangerous. Always respect water and follow safety rules!

slides.title: Fire Safety
slides.content:
# Fire Safety

Fire is useful for cooking and warmth, but it can be very **dangerous** if not handled properly.

## Fire Prevention:
- **Never** play with matches, lighters, or candles
- Keep **flammable materials** away from stoves and heaters
- Do not leave **cooking unattended**
- Check that the **stove is turned off** before leaving the kitchen
- Do not overload **electrical sockets**
- Keep a **fire extinguisher** at home (ask adults)

## What to Do If There Is a Fire:

### The STOP, DROP, and ROLL Rule:
If your clothes catch fire:
1. **STOP** - Do not run (running makes fire worse)
2. **DROP** - Fall to the ground
3. **ROLL** - Roll back and forth to put out the flames

### Escape Plan:
1. **Alert** everyone by shouting "FIRE!"
2. Feel the door - if it is **hot, do not open it**
3. Stay **low** (crawl) because smoke rises
4. Go to the **nearest exit**
5. **Get out** of the building immediately
6. Call the **fire department** from outside
7. **Never go back** inside a burning building

## Fire Safety at Home:
- Have a **fire escape plan** and practice it
- Know **two ways out** of every room
- Have a **meeting point** outside (e.g., the front gate)
- Test **smoke detectors** regularly

## Important Numbers:
- Fire department: **101** (India) / **911** (USA)
- Know your local **emergency number**!

> **Firefighters are heroes!** But the best fire is the one that never starts. Always be careful with fire!

slides.title: Personal Safety
slides.content:
# Personal Safety Rules

Personal safety means protecting yourself from **harm** and **danger** from other people.

## Important Personal Safety Rules:

### 1. Stranger Danger
- **Never** go with a stranger, even if they seem nice
- Do not accept **gifts, candy, or rides** from strangers
- Do not share personal information with **unknown people**
- If a stranger approaches you, go to a **trusted adult** immediately

### 2. Body Safety
- Your body belongs to **YOU**
- No one should touch you in a way that makes you **uncomfortable**
- It is okay to say **"NO"** to any touch you do not like
- Tell a **trusted adult** immediately if someone makes you uncomfortable
- There are **no secrets** about body safety

### 3. Online Safety
- Never share your **name, address, or school** online
- Do not share **photos** with strangers online
- Tell an adult if someone online makes you feel **scared or uncomfortable**
- Do not meet anyone you only know from the **internet**
- Use the internet only with **adult supervision**

### 4. The Buddy System
- Always go places with a **friend** or adult
- Tell your parents **where you are going** and with whom
- Come home **on time** as promised
- If you feel **unsafe**, call your parents immediately

## Trusted Adults:
A trusted adult is someone you can ALWAYS go to for help:
- **Parents** or guardians
- **Teachers**
- **Police officers**
- **Family members** you trust

> **Your Safety Rule:** If something feels WRONG, it probably is. Trust your feelings and tell a trusted adult!

slides.title: Emergency Contacts and First Aid
slides.content:
# Emergency Contacts and Basic First Aid

## Important Emergency Numbers:

| Service | Number (India) | Number (USA/Canada) |
|---------|---------------|--------------------|
| Police | 100 | 911 |
| Fire | 101 | 911 |
| Ambulance | 102 or 108 | 911 |
| Child Helpline | 1098 | 911 |
| Emergency (Universal) | 112 | 911 |

## What to Say in an Emergency Call:
1. Your **name**
2. What **happened**
3. Where you **are** (address or location)
4. Who is **hurt** (if anyone)
5. Stay on the **phone** until told to hang up

## Personal Emergency Information:
Every child should **memorize**:
- Parents' **phone numbers**
- Home **address**
- A neighbor's or relative's **phone number**

## Basic First Aid:

### Small Cut or Scrape:
1. Wash with **clean water**
2. Apply **antiseptic** (if available)
3. Cover with a **bandage**
4. Tell an adult

### Nosebleed:
1. Sit up straight and lean **slightly forward**
2. Pinch the **soft part** of your nose
3. Hold for **10 minutes**
4. Do NOT tilt your head back

### Burns (Minor):
1. Run **cool water** over the burn for 10 minutes
2. Do NOT apply ice, butter, or toothpaste
3. Cover with a clean **cloth**
4. See a doctor for serious burns

### Insect Bite:
1. Wash with soap and water
2. Apply a **cold compress**
3. Do not scratch it
4. Tell an adult if it swells a lot

> **Important:** First aid is for MINOR injuries only. For serious injuries, ALWAYS call emergency services and get adult help!

slides.title: Hygiene Practices - Daily Routine
slides.content:
# Hygiene Practices - Your Daily Routine

**Hygiene** means keeping yourself clean to prevent disease and stay healthy.

## Morning Routine:

### 1. Wake Up and Freshen Up
- Use the **toilet**
- **Wash your face** with clean water

### 2. Brush Your Teeth
- Use a **soft toothbrush** and toothpaste
- Brush for **2 minutes**
- Brush all surfaces - front, back, and top
- **Rinse** your mouth thoroughly
- Brush your **tongue** too!

### 3. Take a Bath
- Use **soap** to clean your body
- Wash your **hair** regularly with shampoo
- Pay attention to: underarms, feet, behind ears, neck
- **Dry** yourself with a clean towel

### 4. Wear Clean Clothes
- Put on **fresh, clean clothes** every day
- Change your **undergarments** daily
- Wear clothes suitable for the **weather**

### 5. Comb Your Hair
- **Brush or comb** your hair neatly
- Keep hair **clean and tidy**

## Throughout the Day:
- Wash hands **before meals** and **after using the toilet**
- **Rinse your mouth** after eating
- Drink plenty of **water**
- Use a **handkerchief** when sneezing or coughing

## Evening/Night Routine:
- **Wash feet** before bed
- **Brush teeth** again before sleeping
- Change into **clean night clothes**

> **Habit Tip:** Do these things at the SAME TIME every day. After 21 days, they become automatic habits!

slides.title: Hand Washing - The Most Important Hygiene Habit
slides.content:
# Hand Washing - Your Best Protection Against Germs!

Washing hands is the **single most important** thing you can do to prevent diseases.

## When Should You Wash Your Hands?

### ALWAYS Wash Hands:
- **Before** eating food
- **After** using the toilet
- **After** playing outside
- **After** touching animals or pets
- **After** sneezing, coughing, or blowing your nose
- **After** handling garbage
- **Before** touching your face (eyes, nose, mouth)
- **After** coming home from outside

## How to Wash Hands Properly:

### The 7 Steps (for 20 seconds):
1. **Wet** your hands with clean water
2. Apply **soap**
3. Rub **palms** together
4. Rub the **back** of each hand
5. Clean **between fingers**
6. Clean **under fingernails**
7. **Rinse** with clean water and **dry** with a clean towel

### How Long?
- Wash for at least **20 seconds**
- That is about the time it takes to sing "Happy Birthday" twice!

## Why Hand Washing Works:
- Germs are **everywhere** - on door handles, desks, phones
- Your hands pick up **millions of germs** every day
- Soap **kills or removes** most germs
- Clean hands = **fewer illnesses**

## Without Hand Washing:
- Germs enter your body through your **mouth, eyes, and nose**
- You can get **cold, flu, stomach infections**
- You can spread germs to **others**

> **Amazing Stat:** Proper hand washing can reduce stomach illnesses by 50% and respiratory infections by 25%! Just by washing your hands!

slides.title: Food and Dental Hygiene
slides.content:
# Food Hygiene and Dental Care

## Food Hygiene:

Eating clean food prevents many diseases.

### Rules for Safe Food:
- **Wash** fruits and vegetables before eating
- Eat **freshly cooked** food whenever possible
- **Cover** food to keep flies and dust away
- Do not eat food that **smells bad or looks old**
- Check **expiry dates** on packaged food
- Store food in **clean containers**
- **Refrigerate** food that can spoil

### Clean Water:
- Drink **boiled, filtered, or packaged** water
- Do not drink water from **unknown sources**
- Carry your own **water bottle** to school

## Dental Hygiene (Teeth Care):

Your teeth are important for **eating, speaking, and smiling**!

### Daily Dental Care:
- Brush **twice a day** (morning and night)
- Use a **pea-sized** amount of fluoride toothpaste
- Brush for at least **2 minutes**
- Replace your toothbrush every **3 months**
- **Floss** between teeth (ask parents to help)

### Foods Good for Teeth:
- **Milk and cheese** - strengthen teeth
- **Crunchy fruits and veggies** - naturally clean teeth
- **Water** - rinses away food particles

### Foods Bad for Teeth:
- **Candy and sweets** - cause cavities
- **Soda and sugary drinks** - damage tooth enamel
- **Sticky foods** - get stuck and cause decay

### Visit the Dentist:
- Go every **6 months** for a check-up
- Do not wait until you have a **toothache**!

> **Smile Bright:** Taking care of your teeth now means a beautiful, healthy smile for life!

slides.title: Preventing Common Diseases
slides.content:
# Preventing Common Diseases Through Hygiene

Good hygiene can prevent many common diseases!

## Common Diseases and Their Prevention:

### Cold and Flu:
- **Cause:** Viruses spread through air and touch
- **Prevention:**
  - Wash hands frequently
  - Cover mouth when coughing/sneezing
  - Avoid close contact with sick people
  - Get enough sleep and eat healthy food

### Stomach Infections:
- **Cause:** Germs in unclean food and water
- **Prevention:**
  - Wash hands before eating
  - Drink clean water
  - Eat freshly cooked food
  - Wash fruits and vegetables

### Skin Infections:
- **Cause:** Fungi and bacteria from dirty skin
- **Prevention:**
  - Bathe daily
  - Wear clean, dry clothes
  - Do not share towels or combs
  - Keep wounds clean and covered

### Eye Infections:
- **Cause:** Germs from dirty hands touching eyes
- **Prevention:**
  - Do not rub eyes with dirty hands
  - Wash face regularly
  - Do not share eye drops

## Vaccinations:
- **Vaccines** protect you from serious diseases
- You get vaccinated as a baby and throughout childhood
- They teach your body to **fight specific diseases**
- Common vaccines: Polio, Measles, Tetanus, Hepatitis

## The Hygiene-Health Connection:

| Good Hygiene Habit | Disease Prevented |
|-------------------|-------------------|
| Hand washing | Cold, flu, stomach infections |
| Brushing teeth | Cavities, gum disease |
| Clean food/water | Cholera, typhoid, dysentery |
| Bathing daily | Skin infections |
| Clean surroundings | Malaria, dengue |

> **Prevention is better than cure!** Simple hygiene habits are your best defense against diseases.

slides.title: Natural Disaster Safety
slides.content:
# Safety During Natural Disasters

Nature can sometimes be unpredictable. Knowing what to do during natural disasters can save lives!

## Earthquake Safety:

### During an Earthquake:
- **Drop, Cover, and Hold On**
- Get under a **strong table or desk**
- Stay away from **windows and glass**
- If outdoors, move to an **open area** away from buildings
- Do NOT use **elevators**

### After an Earthquake:
- Check for **injuries** and help others
- Be prepared for **aftershocks**
- Stay away from **damaged buildings**

## Flood Safety:
- Move to **higher ground** immediately
- Do NOT walk or drive through **flood water**
- Store **emergency supplies** (water, food, flashlight)
- Listen to **official warnings** and instructions

## Thunderstorm Safety:
- Go **indoors** immediately
- Stay away from **tall trees** and metal objects
- Do not use **phones connected to wires**
- Avoid **open fields** and hilltops
- If caught outside, crouch **low** (do not lie flat)

## Cyclone/Hurricane Safety:
- Stay **indoors** in a strong building
- Stay away from **windows**
- Store **water and food** in advance
- Follow **evacuation orders** if given

## Emergency Kit (Keep Ready):
- **Water bottles** and non-perishable food
- **Flashlight** and extra batteries
- **First aid kit**
- **Important documents** in waterproof bag
- **Warm blankets**
- **Whistle** to call for help

> **Be Prepared:** Natural disasters can happen without warning. Having an emergency plan and kit ready can make all the difference!

slides.title: Summary and Key Points
slides.content:
# Summary: Safety and Hygiene

## Safety Rules Summary:

### At Home:
- Be careful with **electricity, fire, and sharp objects**
- Do not open doors to **strangers**
- Know your **emergency contacts**

### At School:
- Walk, do not run in **corridors**
- Follow **playground rules**
- Practice **fire drills**

### On the Road:
- **Look both ways** before crossing
- Use **zebra crossings**
- Wear **seatbelts** in cars and **helmets** on bikes

### Personal Safety:
- Never go with **strangers**
- Tell trusted adults if something feels **wrong**
- Memorize parents' **phone numbers**

## Hygiene Summary:

| Habit | How Often |
|-------|----------|
| Brush teeth | Twice daily |
| Bathe | Daily |
| Wash hands | Many times daily |
| Change clothes | Daily |
| Trim nails | Weekly |
| Dental check-up | Every 6 months |

## Emergency Numbers:
- Police: 100 / 911
- Fire: 101 / 911
- Ambulance: 102 or 108 / 911
- Universal Emergency: 112 / 911

## Key Messages:
1. **Prevention** is better than cure
2. **Clean habits** keep diseases away
3. **Safety rules** prevent accidents
4. Always tell a **trusted adult** when in trouble

> **Congratulations!** You are now a Safety and Hygiene champion. Share these rules with your friends and family to keep everyone safe and healthy!
